body:
## Problem

`designos_apply_spec` could silently accept an instance swap or return a generic create failure when the requested component would be placed through a held-main cycle. Two additional reparent paths (`branch_merge` and live patch replay) could build the same cycle.

## Reproduction

On base `8012e2033a6e1f0dde75ffcc01f43efd33428670`, a synthetic A/B/C component graph produced:

- swap: `Ok(())` even though the link remained and override state could be written;
- create: generic `Failed to create instance`;
- live replay: accepted the reparent without `MOVE_CYCLE`;
- branch merge: accepted a `Reparent` command.

The base-red logs and fixture details are in `mission/design-os-contribution/issue-sweep/issues/968/` in the contribution workspace.

## Root cause

The apply-spec paths checked ordinary ancestry but missed held-main reachability. The merge and replay paths emitted/replayed `Reparent` without calling the shared held-main guard.

## Fix

- Reuse `would_hold_itself` before apply-spec swap/create mutations and return named `INSTANCE_CYCLE`.
- Reject unsafe branch merges with `MergeError::MoveCycle`.
- Reject unsafe live replays with a `MOVE_CYCLE` report.
- Preserve valid swaps, creates, and moves.
- Add regression tests asserting named errors/reports and unchanged serialized state.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p designos-doc --lib --locked` — **PASS** (635 passed)
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — **PASS**
- `cargo clippy -p designos-doc --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — **PASS**
- `git diff --check` — **PASS**
- Independent exact-head review — **PASS (bounded)**, no correctness findings

Full workspace/CI validation is not claimed here; fork workflows require maintainer approval before GitHub jobs can run.

## Scope note

This PR covers the named apply-spec and reparent refusal paths in the issue. The broader dense-tangle growth policy described in the issue discussion remains a follow-up and is intentionally not claimed as solved.

Refs #968
title: fix(doc): name held-main instance cycle refusals
